A.explanation: Force equals rate of change of momentum, $F = (1.5\text{ kg s}^{-1})(20\text{ m s}^{-1}) = 30\text{ N}$ forward on the water, so an equal 30 N backward push must be balanced.

B.explanation: 270 N is too large by a factor of 9 and does not follow from $F = \Delta p/\Delta t$ with $1.5\text{ kg s}^{-1}$ and $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: 1800 N comes from using $90\text{ kg}$ per minute as if per second, $90 \times 20 = 1800$, without converting the time to seconds.

D.explanation: 110000 N is far too large and confuses force with an energy or power type calculation rather than momentum gained per second.

hints: Notice the flow rate is given as 90 kg per minute but force needs mass per second, so convert the time to 60 s.
Think of the horizontal momentum gained by the water each second when it accelerates to $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ on leaving the hose.
Use $F = \Delta p/\Delta t = (\Delta m/\Delta t)v$ with mass per second in $\text{kg s}^{-1}$ and speed in $\text{m s}^{-1}$ to get newtons.
walkthrough: Identify the useful data: mass flow $\Delta m/\Delta t = 90\text{ kg}$ per minute and exit velocity $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ horizontally.
Convert the rate to SI units: $\Delta m/\Delta t = 90/60 = 1.5\text{ kg s}^{-1}$.
State the rule: force on the water equals its rate of gain of momentum, $F = \Delta p/\Delta t = (\Delta m/\Delta t)v$.
Substitute with units: $F = (1.5\text{ kg s}^{-1})(20\text{ m s}^{-1}) = 30\text{ kg m s}^{-2} = 30\text{ N}$.
By Newton's third law the water pushes back on the hose with 30 N, so the person must supply at least 30 N forwards. This is option A.
